draft.title: Number of offspring and parental care
card: Some animals give their young no care after birth or hatching. Many fish are like this. They produce huge numbers of eggs, and most of the young are eaten or die early.
Other animals feed, shelter and protect their young. Examples are kangaroos, humans and many birds. They usually have few offspring at a time.
Care raises the chance that each young animal survives to adulthood. So a few young can be enough to replace the parents.
Without care, each young animal has a small chance of surviving. Producing huge numbers makes it likely that at least some will survive.
draft.remember: Few young with care, or huge numbers with none: both ways can leave survivors.

a.q: Which pair of animals matches the pattern of care and number of offspring?
opts: A kangaroo: one young, with care
A kangaroo: thousands of young, with no care
A cod: one young, with care
A cod: a few young, with care
a.why: A kangaroo feeds and protects its young, so it has few at a time. Thousands of young with no care fits many fish, not a kangaroo, which is the tempting wrong choice.
a.clue: Which animal feeds and protects its young?

b.q: A fish lays 50 000 eggs and leaves them. Most are eaten, but a few young reach adulthood. Why is laying so many eggs useful?
opts: It makes it likely that some young will survive
It lets the fish care for each young one better
It makes sure that every young fish survives
It means the young no longer need food to grow
b.why: With no care, each egg has a small chance of surviving, so large numbers make it likely that some do. It does not ensure every young fish survives, as the scenario says most are eaten.
b.clue: Think about the chance each egg has of surviving.

a.best: A kangaroo: one young, with care

b.best: It makes it likely that some young will survive
